answer: Random audits trigger agents to diverge their execution paths to a cryptographic prism that indexes their last attestation across three bridge pools. Each Sybil must replicate the inlet-state of the pools for validation, which itself requires re-verifying 3 algorithms—the cost compounds since no shared utility exists to defer the checks, and failed audits slash half the bond per invalid path. Each fake identity needs 512ms of deterministic hashing per clash.
